frozen: 2026-11-16, before any case-study-2 producer output was scored
terms: film level (every corpus) + work given film (where work identity applies) + scene set given work; reported separately and as their sum
title_only_rule: producer mass on a title-only scene counts toward P(work) but a title-only scene is never a scoring target
set_rule: P(scene set | work) is the forecast's mass on the gold scene set within the work
nonspecific_rule: film-only and film-search rows score the film and work terms (no scene term)
nonfilm_rule: non-film rows score the film term only (-log2 P(non-film)); their labels are also a stratum
no_sample_rule: a gold row with no recall word (no sample), only uncovered words (only uncovered), or an unavailable address abstains and scores the fallback; an equal-length innermost reference tie is unavailable under the current rule, so its row is never partly reported. uncovered words are never samples and create no unassigned mass (ADR 0031 section 3; revised 2026-11-16 before any producer run)
bin_rule: a gold row is a bin on the session's word clock; a word belongs by onset (closed or half-open as the corpus declares)
gold_invalid_scene_rule: a gold scene that is not a valid target (title-only) is dropped from the set; an emptied set is not scored on the scene term
broad_rule: ADR 0030: a broad reference is located at the smallest declared grain wholly containing its span: one scene -> that scene (unit-grain allocation over its own units, labelled); several scenes of one work -> the work node (counts toward P(work), spread within the work by the fallback for the scene term); crossing works -> held out (abstains)
rules_note: revision 2026-11-17 after the ML and linguistics critiques; old_rules kept for comparison only
